papers.title: Adolescent digital intimate partner violence: A call for global policy strategies.
papers.abstract: Digital technologies have become a fundamental part of adolescent communication and romantic relationships across the globe. While technology enables adolescents to feel more connected, it also introduces new ways to perpetrate and experience intimate partner violence (IPV). This paper synthesizes emerging evidence about global digital IPV to critically examine the current state of knowledge about adolescent digital IPV and make recommendations for the incorporation of digital IPV into global-level frameworks. We identify that although there are many similarities to in-person IPV, unique digital affordances, such as absence of interpersonal cues, lack of immediate social feedback, remote surveillance, permanence, and anonymity, create a new context to perpetrate and experience IPV, which may exacerbate psychological and developmental harm and complicate prevention and intervention. Despite this, digital adolescent IPV is missing from global frameworks that critically influence policy, funding, and research. Global frameworks should incorporate the unique challenges of digital adolescent IPV by establishing a specific taxonomy, creating a global research agenda, and developing guiding principles for prevention and intervention. Recommended guiding principles for policy and practice include prioritizing recognition of adolescents as a high-risk population, respect for adolescent participation in digital platforms while teaching digital competence, co-creation with adolescents, and partnership with technology platforms to affect change at the design-level. This paper concludes that global frameworks for digital adolescent IPV are critical in order to mobilize coordinated research, evidence-based programming, and adolescent-centered policies to combat digital IPV and develop technology to foster resilience and healthy relationship development worldwide.

papers.title: The Use of Palaeoecology in UK Peatland Restoration: Perspectives From Practice.
papers.abstract: Extensive degradation has necessitated high-priority restoration of UK peatland ecosystems. Palaeoecology has great potential to support peatland restoration, offering a long-term perspective of environmental change that can help determine baseline conditions, restoration targets, and intervention success. However, it is suggested by palaeoenvironmental researchers that palaeoecology is underutilised in practical settings, with few examples of applied palaeoecological studies within academic literature. This study uses a practice perspective to evaluate the extent to which palaeoecology is incorporated into UK peatland restoration and identifies barriers and opportunities for integrating long-term ecological research into restoration practice. A desk-based study of 68 UK peatland restoration projects and survey of 32 peatland practitioners were used to explore the use of palaeoecological research as part of UK peatland restoration projects. A total of 10 instances of applied palaeoecology in UK peatland restoration were found between the desk-based study and practitioner survey. The findings indicate that palaeoecology is rarely utilised in UK peatland restoration practice, with limitations in funding, time, and academic input identified as key barriers. Cases where palaeoecology has been considered primarily utilised pollen analysis and radiocarbon dating, with practitioners largely involved in fieldwork and research design. This study makes two recommendations to facilitate the incorporation of palaeoecological research into UK peatland restoration practice: (i) better dissemination and documentation of case studies to provide greater evidence of how palaeoecology may be used to support UK peatland restoration and clearer insight into the use of palaeoecology in practice; (ii) better two-way knowledge transfer between palaeoecologists and practitioners to identify restoration challenges and knowledge gaps where palaeoecology could contribute.

papers.title: MicroRNA as Biomarker For Neuroprognostication following Cardiac Arrest: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate prognostication of neurologic outcomes after cardiac arrest (CA) remains challenging due to a shortage of robust predictors. An ideal biomarker should directly reflect the prognosis-defining injury and allow for objective, reproducible measurement through standardized assays. MicroRNAs (miRs) are promising candidates because of their close relationship to cellular metabolism, high stability, and detectability across multiple body fluids. METHODS: To evaluate the current evidence for potential clinical utility of miRs in neuroprognostication after CA, we conducted a systematic literature search across MEDLINE, EMBASE, SCOPUS, and The Cochrane Library through July 2025 using predefined keywords related to microRNA, cardiac arrest, and prognostication. Two independent reviewers screened and selected studies according to predefined inclusion criteria, and relevant data were compiled into a structured dataset. RESULTS: Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria, reporting on 28 distinct miRs across 3021 samples. Among these, miR-124 was the most frequently studied, while miR-122, miR-9, miR-21, miR-574, and miR-483 were each investigated in more than one study. Methodological approaches varied, and reporting was not uniform across studies. Prognostic performance was expressed using different metrics, including odds ratios, area under the curve (AUC), and mean group differences. MiR-124 was the most extensively evaluated candidate, with the highest reported AUC of 0.89 (95% CI 0.80-0.97) at 48 hours post-ROSC for poor prognosis. However, this was not uniformly reproduced across studies and will require external validation. DISCUSSION: Evidence supporting specific miRs as prognostic biomarkers after cardiac arrest is thus growing but remains limited in scope and weakened by heterogeneity in study design and reporting. papers.title: Courting the P value: An academic's love affair with statistical significance.
papers.abstract: This satirical commentary uses the metaphor of a courtship to examine the academic preoccupation with P < 0.05, highlighting how the pursuit of statistical significance can encourage analytical flexibility and confusion between statistical and clinical importance. It advocates a more mature approach to surgical research in which P values are interpreted alongside effect estimates, confidence intervals, study quality, evidence robustness and, ultimately, relevance to patients.

papers.title: A large orca from the Lower Pleistocene of the Southern North Sea Basin pushes back the origin of macropredatory behavior in the oceanic dolphins (Odontoceti, Delphinidae).
papers.abstract: The evolutionary history of the biggest extant top predator of our planet, the killer whale Orcinus orca, remains poorly understood. Currently, the fossil record of the genus Orcinus includes only a single formally recognized extinct species, the small-bodied (3.5 meters) piscivorous Orcinus citoniensis from the Pliocene of Cetona, Italy. Here we describe and refer to Orcinus sp., five delphinid fossil remains from the Pleistocene of the southern North Sea, consisting of two fragmentary crania, an incomplete mandible and two atlas-axis cervical complexes. Regression analyses based on extant Orcinus orca measurements and 3D model comparisons indicate an estimated body length between 7.2 and 7.7 m, comparable to that of the largest living male killer whales. Palynological dating of the sediment of one cranial specimen supports a Gelasian (2.6-2.1 Ma) age. This large representative of the genus Orcinus displays morphological features - including large, deep, and widely separated alveoli and deeply excavated condylar fossae - indicating macroraptorial feeding abilities. Orcinus sp. represents the largest Pleistocene delphinid yet documented and provides the earliest known evidence for the emergence of macroraptorial predation within Delphinidae, substantially predating the Middle Pleistocene divergence of modern killer whale ecotypes inferred from genomic data. By demonstrating that this feeding strategy was established more than two million years ago, our results underscore both the long-term stability of apex predation in marine ecosystems and its potential vulnerability to rapid human-induced environmental change.

papers.title: A new species of Taenia from Brandt's vole in the Hulunbuir grassland of China: mitogenomic characterization, phylogenetic position and evolutionary origin.
papers.journal: International journal for parasitology. Parasites and wildlife
papers.abstract: Taeniid cestodes include important zoonotic parasites whose larval stages infect a wide range of mammalian intermediate hosts, creating transmission risks across wildlife, domestic animals and humans. However, taeniids infecting rodents in northern Asian grasslands remain incompletely documented. Here, we describe a new species of taeniid Taenia hulunbuirensis n. sp., based on cysticerci recovered from Brandt's voles (Lasiopodomys brandtii Radde, 1861) in the Hulunbuir grassland of Inner Mongolia, China. The rostellum of its larva bore 62-68 hooks, with large hooks measuring 230-245 μm and small hooks 138-148 μm long. We sequenced and characterized its mitogenome, obtaining a complete circular molecule of 13,582 bp with an organization consistent with typical taeniid mitogenomes. Maximum-likelihood analysis of the concatenated 12 mitochondrial protein-coding genes placed T. hulunbuirensis n. sp. as the sister species of T. tianguangfui, while nuclear 18S rRNA phylogeny independently recovered the same relationship. Despite this close relationship, T. hulunbuirensis n. sp. differed from T. tianguangfui by p-distances of 5.34 % for cox1, 6.40 % for nad1 and 6.49 % across the 12-PCG alignment. Molecular dating estimated their divergence at 1.575 Mya (95 % highest posterior density: 1.312-1.823 Mya). This estimate overlaps the inferred origin of Lasiopodomys at approximately 1.79 Mya, suggesting that early Pleistocene vole diversification may have facilitated host switching or host-associated isolation. This discovery expands the known diversity of taeniids infecting rodents in the eastern Central Asian steppe and suggests that geographic and habitat isolation associated with Qinghai-Tibet Plateau uplift contributed to tapeworm diversification.

papers.title: Atropisomerization of 1,1'-Bi-2-naphthol through Hydrogen-Bond-Acceptor-Coupled Cu(I) Catalysis.
papers.abstract: A mild and efficient catalytic system has been developed for the atropisomerization of 1,1'-bi-2-naphthol (BINOL) using an ion-pairing copper(I) complex, [Cu(bcp)2][CuCl2] (bcp = bathocuproine). This catalyst operates under neutral conditions at room temperature and lowers the rotation barrier through a unique mechanism involving hydrogen-bonding and π-stacking interactions, as elucidated by experimental and computational studies. These features render the atropisomerization compatible with kinetic resolution and enable homogeneous non-enzymatic dynamic kinetic resolution of BINOL. Sequential atropisomerization and enantiomeric enrichment enable controlled inversion of axial chirality, offering potential strategies for the design of chemically driven molecular motors.

papers.title: Elucidating the structure-crystal packing-weak interaction-collective vibration relationship governing terahertz spectral fingerprints of vitamin C stereoisomers.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Vitamin C (l-ascorbic acid) and its stereoisomer D-isoascorbic acid possess nearly identical molecular compositions but distinct physicochemical properties, making their discrimination and structural interpretation challenging. In this study, the terahertz spectral features of l-ascorbic acid and D-isoascorbic acid were systematically investigated using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy combined with periodic density functional theory calculations. Experimental THz absorption spectra in the range of 0.5-2.5 THz were obtained and reproduced by theoretical calculations, confirming the reliability of the crystal models. To further validate the weak absorption features and the crystal structure models, low-temperature (77 K) terahertz measurements were performed to confirm the authenticity of the weak peaks, while powder X-ray diffraction patterns were collected to verify the crystal structure models and the crystallographic parameters used in the calculations. The Vibrational Mode Automatic Relevance Determination method was employed to quantitatively identify the vibrational origins of THz absorption peaks, while Interaction Region Indicator and Hirshfeld Surface analyses were used to characterize intermolecular weak interactions within the crystals. The results demonstrate that the THz absorptions of both stereoisomers mainly originate from collective lattice vibrations involving coupled bond-angle bending and dihedral torsional motions. Although van der Waals interactions dominate both crystal systems, D-isoascorbic acid exhibits stronger hydrogen-bonding interactions and distinct intermolecular interaction networks. The stereochemical differences lead to different crystal packing arrangements, which regulate weak interactions, modify restoring forces, and influence collective vibrational coupling, ultimately determining the THz spectral fingerprints. papers.title: Cognitive-behavioral conjoint therapy for posttraumatic stress disorder: A systematic review of outcomes, mechanisms, and clinical applications.
papers.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with interpersonal dysfunction, and including loved ones in treatment may benefit both PTSD symptom reduction and relationship functioning. Cognitive-behavioral conjoint therapy (CBCT) for PTSD is a manualized, trauma-focused psychotherapy delivered in a dyadic format, typically to an individual with PTSD and their intimate partner. We replicated and extended a systematic review published in 2020 to incorporate several studies published since then. Procedures for this preregistered systematic review were consistent with PRISMA guidelines. We identified 50 reports representing 41 unique studies: 19 main outcome studies (i.e., five randomized controlled trials [RCTs], four of which were published after the previous review; 12 uncontrolled trials; and two naturalistic outcome studies), 17 secondary analyses, and five ongoing RCTs. Overall, these studies indicate that CBCT for PTSD and its adaptations improve PTSD symptoms. Findings were mixed for relationship satisfaction, co-occurring psychiatric symptoms, and partner accommodation. Baseline relationship satisfaction moderated effects of CBCT for PTSD on relationship outcomes; partner accommodation and social support moderated PTSD outcomes. Adaptations designed to increase efficiency, accessibility, and potency include alternative formats of treatment delivery, modified content, and pharmacological augmentation. The evidence base for CBCT for PTSD has grown rapidly in recent years, but methodological limitations, including small sample sizes, insufficient evidence from well-controlled trials, lack of generalizability of samples, and limited evidence of mechanisms of action, remain. Several ongoing studies were designed and will be well-positioned to address these limitations.

papers.title: Experience with continuous glucose monitoring in reducing diabetes management burden for older Chinese Americans with cognitive impairment.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: We aimed to study the experience of using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) among older Chinese Americans with cognitive impairment (CI) and their care partners. We also explored physicians' perspectives on using CGM in older adults with cognitive decline. BACKGROUND: CI can heighten the challenges of managing type 2 diabetes (T2D), particularly among older Chinese Americans due to the interplays of cultural, financial, and health-related burdens and older adults with cognitive decline that add additional challenges of diabetes management. The application of CGM in such populations remains understudied. METHOD: Older Chinese American adults with CI and T2D and their care partners were recruited from the New York City (NYC) community. Clinicians who had clinical experience of the application of CGM in individuals with diabetes and cognitive decline were recruited nationally. After brief education, patients used CGM for 10 days and shared the data with their care partners. In-depth interviews were conducted among older Chinese Americans with both T2D and CI (n = 11), care partners (n = 11), and clinicians (n = 8), transcribed, and then thematically analyzed using ATLAS.ti software. RESULTS: Older Chinese Americans with both T2D and CI had a mean age of 74.5 ± 5.2 years, and 63.6% were women. They reported CGM helped them assess the influence of various foods on glucose levels in order to choose appropriate foods (n = 10) and portion sizes (n = 5), gain insight on the role and impact of exercise (n = 5), enhance care partner involvement (n = 5) and communication (n = 4), and promote a positive mindset by improving management confidence or disease understanding (n = 9) in diabetes self-management. papers.title: Caregiver-provider relationship quality and health outcomes in family caregivers of people living with dementia.
papers.journal: The journals of gerontology. Series B, Psychological sciences and social sciences
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Family caregivers of individuals with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) work with healthcare providers to ensure effective care coordination on behalf of the care recipient. However, challenges within the caregiver-healthcare provider relationship are common and may contribute to poor caregiver health outcomes. This study examined the impact of the perceived quality of the relationship between family caregivers and healthcare providers and the caregivers' daily mental health symptom burden (depressive symptoms, anxiety, and stress). METHODS: The study included 228 family caregivers who lived with and provided unpaid care to a family member with dementia. Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LMM) were developed to assess whether the caregiver-provider relationship was associated with caregiver daily depressive symptoms, daily anxiety, and daily stress. RESULTS: Of 228 caregivers, 82% were female, 84% were spouses or partners of the care recipient, and 9% of caregivers were classified as living in poverty. Caregivers who rated their providers' affect (perceptions of being valued, respected, and emotionally supported) more positively reported lower daily depressive symptoms (β = -0.06, p = .001) and anxiety symptoms (β = -0.07, p < .001). The caregiver-provider relationship was not associated with daily stress experiences. DISCUSSION: Findings from the study suggest that healthcare provider affect (perceptions of being valued, respected, and emotionally supported) may be a protective factor, especially against depressive symptoms and anxiety, and offer an avenue for future interventions. Integrating caregiver-provider relationship-informed practices into routine dementia care may help foster emotionally responsive, person- and family-centered care.

papers.title: Cost-effectiveness of a digital parenting intervention for reducing violence and related health burden among adolescents in Tanzania.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Violence against children is a major global public health concern associated with substantial physical and mental health burden across the life course. Parenting interventions are effective in preventing violence against children, yet evidence on their cost-effectiveness, particularly for digitally delivered programmes in low-resource settings, remains limited. We evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a blended-digital parenting intervention in Tanzania. METHODS: We conducted cost-effectiveness and cost-benefit analyses alongside a cluster-randomised controlled trial of ParentApp for Teens delivered to caregivers and adolescents aged 10-17 years. Trial outcomes were combined with programme cost data to estimate delivery costs at scale. Cost-effectiveness ratios (CERs) were calculated as cost per incident averted using incidence risk ratios from 14-month follow-up data. A discounted CER approach proportionally allocated intervention costs across multiple outcomes. Cost-benefit analysis compared prevention costs with immediate public-sector labour costs associated with formal case response. RESULTS: The intervention achieved significant reductions in multiple violence outcomes, including adolescent sexual violence victimisation, child maltreatment, and caregiver intimate partner violence-forms of violence associated with substantial health consequences. Using observed RCT implementation expenditure of US$69.02 per enrolled dyad, estimated costs per incident averted were US$30.83 for adolescent sexual violence, US$5.43 for child maltreatment and US$12.03 for caregiver IPV. Under a prospective routine-delivery scenario of just under US$6 per dyad at n = 10,000, corresponding CERs were US$2.67, US$0.47 and US$1.04, respectively. At scale, routine delivery was estimated at approximately US$6 per caregiver-adolescent dyad, compared with an estimated US$121.10 in immediate labour costs for a reported case entering formal response.
